set.descent_text: The route finishes on easy snow and ice slopes to the summit of Colfax Peak, and the way down is a walk-off with no rappels. Cross the Colfax-Baker col behind the summit and pick up the standard Coleman-Deming route down the Coleman Glacier, as for the neighboring routes on this face. Stay roped for the glacier and expect the same crevasses you passed on the way in. Follow the lateral moraine to the Heliotrope Ridge Trail and the trailhead, and leave daylight for the glacier, since descending it late is slow and hazardous.

review.notes: Route tops out by simul-climbing snow and neve to the Colfax summit, then a walk-off the back of the peak to the car (Alpinist, Haley). Colfax-Baker col and Coleman-Deming glacier descent taken from the Cosley-Houston/Polish Route descent facts in the app on the same face and Haley's photo captions.

set.descent_text: This variation leaves the Cave Route at the top of its first pitch and rejoins it, so the descent is the Cave Route's: rappel from the west side of the summit. The usual rappel there takes two ropes, but they can jam on the pull, and a mid-height station lets parties make it with one rope. The rappel lands on a ledge. Move climber's right to a second rappel that follows the first pitch of the North Face down to the saddle shared with Liberty Bell. From the notch, reverse the approach down the gully and through the bowl to the Blue Lake Trail.
set.approach: From the Blue Lake Trailhead on SR 20 near Washington Pass, hike the Blue Lake Trail about 1.5 miles to a small meadow, then take the climbers' path that breaks off just past a small stream and climbs slabs, talus and heather to the gully between Liberty Bell and Concord Tower. The gully holds snow into early summer, so an ice axe helps early in the season, and rockfall is a concern once it melts out. From the notch, drop about 50 feet down the gully on the north side of the tower to the two diagonal cracks that start the Cave Route. This variation begins at the top of that route's first pitch, so the base of the climb is the same.

review.notes: Variation starts at the top of Cave Route P1 and links its last two pitches (MP). Cave Route page gives the west-side summit rappel, ledge, then second rappel down the North Face P1 to the notch, and the base/approach; North Face page confirms Blue Lake Trail and climbers' trail up the gully.
